raw_text:
This is uncomplicated, nonsevere unilateral AOM with a definite diagnosis. At exactly 24 months, temperature <39°C and mild otalgia <48 hours, either immediate treatment or observation is guideline-concordant. I would offer shared-decision observation if reliable follow-up is available.

Analgesia: acetaminophen 160 mg (5 mL of 160 mg/5 mL) PO q4–6h PRN, or ibuprofen 10 mg/kg/dose = 124 mg (6.2 mL of 100 mg/5 mL) PO q6–8h PRN while well hydrated. Use one agent as needed; avoid duplicate acetaminophen-containing products.

Observation plan: fluids, sleep/comfort measures, no decongestants or antihistamines. Call/reassess sooner for worsening; start antibiotics if not clearly improving within 48–72 hours.

Give a safety-net prescription or arrange prompt follow-up:

Amoxicillin 400 mg/5 mL: 7 mL PO BID for 7 days (≈90 mg/kg/day).

This is appropriate because there is no amoxicillin in the past 30 days, purulent conjunctivitis, or penicillin allergy. If any of those emerge, use high-dose amoxicillin-clavulanate instead.

Return urgently for toxic appearance, poor intake/dehydration, uncontrolled pain, new otorrhea, persistent fever ≥39°C, or postauricular erythema/swelling, pinna displacement, or mastoid tenderness.

Immediate amoxicillin is also entirely reasonable if the parent prefers it, follow-up is uncertain, or symptoms worsen. AAP guidance supports observation for nonsevere unilateral AOM at this age and identifies high-dose amoxicillin as first-line when treating. AAP guideline
, AAP quick reference
